newsitem.title: USA: U.S. citizens on hijacked Ethiopian plane.
newsitem.headline: U.S. citizens on hijacked Ethiopian plane.

text.p: U.S. citizens were aboard the hijacked Ethiopian Airlines Boeing 767 that crashed into the Indian Ocean on Saturday, but their fate was not immediately clear, the State Department said.
Spokesman Christopher Bush said "several" Americans were among the 175 passengers and crew, but he could not say how many or if any of them were among the 50 survivors found so far.

"Until we've obtained accurate information we will have no other details," he said. Ethiopian Airlines said it would release a passenger list on Sunday. Of the 50 bodies found so far, most were Asians and Africans.

The pilot and one crew member were among those who survived when the plane, hijacked between Addis Ababa and the Kenyan capital Nairobi, ran out of fuel and crashed into the sea as it tried to land at Moroni Airport in the Comoro Islands.
The identity of the hijackers has not been released but they reportedly ordered the pilot to fly to Australia.

Bush said the United States was sending an interagency team to obtain information about and provide assistance to the American passengers, including State Department representatives and National Transportation Safety Board officials. The group also would be available to support Comoran authorities.
Agents of the Federal Bureau of Investigation would accompany the team and offer their help with investigations, Bush said.
Because the aircraft was hijacked with American citizens aboard, the incident amounts to air piracy under U.S. law.
Two hijackers have been brought to the United States for trial for a crime committed overseas in which Americans were victims.

In July, Palestinian Omar Mohammed Ali Rezaq was found guilty in a U.S. federal court of the 1985 hijacking of an Egypt Air jet in which 58 people died. He was one of three men who hijacked the Cairo-bound plane after it left Athens and later shot three Israelis and two Americans in the head in an attempt to persuade authorities in Malta to refuel the aircraft.

Fawaz Yunis, a Lebanese who was snatched by FBI agents in 1987 from a boat in the Mediterranean, was convicted for his role in the 1985 hijacking of a Jordanian airliner with two Amnericans on board and is serving a 30-year sentence in a U.S. prison.
